summary: A worker given an agreement in a rush asks for more time in writing and marks the deadlines.
realLife: The EEOC advises noting the deadline as soon as you get the agreement, asking for clarification of confusing terms, requesting more time in writing if rushed, and considering a lawyer.
sources: U.S. EEOC, Q&A on waivers of discrimination claims in severance agreements: https://www.eeoc.gov/laws/guidance/qa-understanding-waivers-discrimination-claims-employee-severance-agreements
inGame: needs: severance agreements; the request is a choice on the termination meeting. Scene: needs a producer for layoff-terms.

turns.summary: The employer agrees in writing to the extra days.
turns.writesBack: The deadline moves, and the person signs after review.

turns.summary: The employer says the paper must be signed by the date shown.
turns.writesBack: The person signs under pressure or walks away, and the tie to the employer cools.

turns.summary: The person signs on the spot without asking for more time.
turns.writesBack: Terms are fixed at once, and regret may follow later.
